acceptedAnswer.text: A Junior ADU (JADU) is a specific type of accessory dwelling unit that is always contained within the existing walls of a single-family home. It must be no more than 500 square feet, include an efficiency kitchen, and have its own separate exterior entrance. JADUs are often created by converting existing space, such as a bedroom or a portion of a garage, within the primary residence. This can be a cost-effective way to add housing or rental income to a property.
